translationRepairs: The next year, when the crown prince was to be enfeoffed, the chief ministers memorialized that the full ceremonial guard should be prepared to announce the event at the ancestral temple. The emperor said: "Previously, when I received my honorific title and made the thanksgiving visit, you had me follow only Emperor Zhenzong of Song's precedent—court dress and riding a horse—which was very light in ritual terms. Why should the crown prince now receive the full ceremonial treatment?"

The next year, when the crown prince was to be invested, the chief ministers memorialized that the full ceremonial guard should be prepared to announce the event at the ancestral temple. The emperor said: "Previously, when I received my honorific title and made the thanksgiving visit, you had me follow only Emperor Zhenzong of Song's precedent—court dress and riding a horse—which was very light in ritual terms. Why should the crown prince now receive the full ceremonial treatment?"
冊皇太子 names documentary investiture of the heir; enfeoffed misreads 冊 as a landed grant, and invested restores the rite named in the sentence.
They all wore flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet embroidered udumbara-flower shirts, leather belts, silver-brown baggy trousers, brocade serpent sashes, and bore ceremonial blades.
They all wore flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet embroidered baoxiang-flower shirts, leather belts, silver-brown baggy trousers, brocade serpent sashes, and bore ceremonial blades.
緋繡寶相花衫 names the baoxiang floral motif; udumbara would require 優曇, which is not in the unit.
All wore flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet embroidered udumbara-flower shirts, leather belts, silver-brown baggy trousers, brocade serpent sashes, and bore ceremonial blades.
All wore flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet embroidered baoxiang-flower shirts, leather belts, silver-brown baggy trousers, brocade serpent sashes, and bore ceremonial blades.
The same 寶相花 shirts are misread as udumbara; baoxiang-flower is the source motif.
One hundred eighty long-march guards wore iron armor and helmets, red brocade vests and brocade arm guards, rode armored horses with red brocade tail covers, and bore golden lances.
One hundred eight long-march guards wore iron armor and helmets, red brocade vests and brocade arm guards, rode armored horses with red brocade tail covers, and bore golden lances.
長行一百八人 is 108 men; 180 would need 一百八十, and 18 cadre plus 108 matches the 126 of the golden-lance company.
One hundred eighty long-march guards, iron armor, helmets, red brocade vests, brocade arm guards, armored horses with red brocade tail covers, bearing golden lances.
One hundred eight long-march guards, iron armor, helmets, red brocade vests, brocade arm guards, armored horses with red brocade tail covers, bearing golden lances.
一百八人 is 108, not 180; the numeral in the Chinese is unambiguous.
Silver Lance company: 126 men, with eighteen cadre and one hundred eighty long-march guards dressed as above, bearing silver lances.
Silver Lance company: 126 men, with eighteen cadre and one hundred eight long-march guards dressed as above, bearing silver lances.
銀槍隊一百二十六人 with 人員十八 and 長行一百八人 is 18 plus 108, not 180 long-march guards.
Silver Lance company, 126 men, with eighteen cadre and one hundred eighty long-march guards; dress as above, with silver lances.
Silver Lance company, 126 men, with eighteen cadre and one hundred eight long-march guards; dress as above, with silver lances.
長行一百八人 is 108, which with eighteen cadre totals the stated 126.
Great Tranquility palanquin: 181 men, including two directors of the imperial carriage service, two vice directors of the palace service, and two tribute officers, all in official dress.
Great Tranquility palanquin: 181 men, including two directors of the imperial carriage service, two vice directors of the palace service, and two fengzhi officials, all in official dress.
奉職官 is the Jin fengzhi rank among the palanquin officers; tribute officers would be a different office and is not in the Chinese.
Great Tranquility palanquin, 181 men: including two directors of the imperial carriage service, two vice directors of the palace service, and two tribute officers, all in official dress.
Great Tranquility palanquin, 181 men: including two directors of the imperial carriage service, two vice directors of the palace service, and two fengzhi officials, all in official dress.
The same 奉職官二人 are fengzhi officials, not tribute officers.
Four palanquin attendants wore military caps, yellow embroidered udumbara-flower shirts, silver-brown waist bands, and baggy trousers.
Four palanquin attendants wore military caps, yellow embroidered baoxiang-flower shirts, silver-brown waist bands, and baggy trousers.
黃繡寶相花衫 is baoxiang embroidery, not the udumbara flower.
Four palanquin attendants, military caps, yellow embroidered udumbara-flower shirts, silver-brown waist bands, and baggy trousers.
Four palanquin attendants, military caps, yellow embroidered baoxiang-flower shirts, silver-brown waist bands, and baggy trousers.
The literal field repeats the same 寶相花 error; baoxiang-flower matches the source.

In the sixth month of Mingchang 5 (1194), the Ministry of Works memorialized, "In Dading 6, when Emperor Shizong returned from the Western Capital, he adopted the Song ritual for a provincial inspection's return to the capital, employing a yellow-banner guard of two thousand men together with the jade and golden carriages, five hundred armored horsemen of the wickerwork company, and forty-two imperial escort officers; thereafter this formation was not used again.

In the sixth month of Mingchang 5 (1194), the Department of State Affairs memorialized, "In Dading 6, when Emperor Shizong returned from the Western Capital, he adopted the Song ritual for a provincial inspection's return to the capital, employing a yellow-banner guard of two thousand men together with the jade and golden carriages, five hundred armored horsemen of the wickerwork company, and forty-two imperial escort officers; thereafter this formation was not used again.
尚書省奏 is a memorial from the Department of State Affairs; 工部 is not named.

In the sixth month of the fifth year of Mingchang under Emperor Zhangzong, the Ministry of Works memorialized: "In the sixth year of Dading, when Emperor Shizong returned from the Western Capital, adopting the Song ritual for returning to the capital after inspecting the provinces, he used a yellow-banner armed guard of 2,000 men, together with the jade and golden carriages, 500 armored horsemen of the wickerwork company, and 42 imperial escort officers; thereafter it was no longer used.

In the sixth month of the fifth year of Mingchang under Emperor Zhangzong, the Department of State Affairs memorialized: "In the sixth year of Dading, when Emperor Shizong returned from the Western Capital, adopting the Song ritual for returning to the capital after inspecting the provinces, he used a yellow-banner armed guard of 2,000 men, together with the jade and golden carriages, 500 armored horsemen of the wickerwork company, and 42 imperial escort officers; thereafter it was no longer used.
The literal likewise mistranslates 尚書省 as the Ministry of Works; Department of State Affairs is the named body.
In Cheng'an 1 (1196), provincial ministers memorialized, "For the great Southern Suburb rite, the Grand Carriage Guard of Honor should employ 21,218 men and 8,198 horses.
In Cheng'an 1 (1196), the ministers of the Department of State Affairs memorialized, "For the great Southern Suburb rite, the Grand Carriage Guard of Honor should employ 21,218 men and 8,198 horses.
省臣奏 continues the Shangshu Sheng ministers of the preceding memorials, not provincial (外省) ministers.

In Taihe 6 (1206), when the emperor wished to perform the joint ancestral sacrifice in person, he ordered the relevant offices to calculate the costs. The Ministry of Works memorialized, "The guard would require three thousand five hundred men, more than ten thousand strings of cash, and eight hundred sixty-five horses.

In Taihe 6 (1206), when the emperor wished to perform the joint ancestral sacrifice in person, he ordered the relevant offices to calculate the costs. The Department of State Affairs memorialized, "The guard would require three thousand five hundred men, more than ten thousand strings of cash, and eight hundred sixty-five horses.
尚書省奏 again names the Department of State Affairs, not the Ministry of Works.

In the sixth year of Taihe, when the emperor wished to perform the joint ancestral sacrifice in person, he ordered the relevant offices to calculate the labor costs. The Ministry of Works memorialized: "The armed guard should use 3,500 men, more than 10,000 strings of cash, and 865 horses.

In the sixth year of Taihe, when the emperor wished to perform the joint ancestral sacrifice in person, he ordered the relevant offices to calculate the labor costs. The Department of State Affairs memorialized: "The armed guard should use 3,500 men, more than 10,000 strings of cash, and 865 horses.
The literal has the same 尚書省 misidentification; the replacement restores the memorializing office.
Next came the tribute palace women.
Next came the palace women in attendance.
供奉宮人 are palace women serving in attendance in the cortege, not tribute women.
供奉 here is attendance service; tribute is unsupported.

Twelve guide officers: two palace secretaries, two moral instructors, two crown prince sons, two grand mentors, one grand preceptor, one grand tutor, one grand protector, and one junior preceptor behind the golden carriage.

Twelve guide officers: two palace secretaries, two moral instructors, two shuzi, two supervisors of the household, one grand preceptor, one grand tutor, one grand protector, and one junior preceptor behind the golden carriage.
庶子二人 are Eastern Palace shuzi officers and 詹事二人 supervisors of the heir's household, not the crown prince's sons or grand mentors (太師 already appears separately).

Twelve guide officers: two palace secretaries, two moral instructors, two crown prince sons, two grand mentors, one grand preceptor, one grand tutor, one grand protector, and one junior preceptor behind the golden carriage.

Twelve guide officers: two palace secretaries, two moral instructors, two shuzi, two supervisors of the household, one grand preceptor, one grand tutor, one grand protector, and one junior preceptor behind the golden carriage.
The same office list is restored: 庶子 as shuzi and 詹事 as household supervisors.

First positive rank: the Three Excellencies of Tutor, Preceptor, and Protector; the Three Dukes; and the Director of the Department of State Affairs—each with ten vermilion-robed direct attendants; the Three Dukes' attendants were called Direct Office.

First positive rank: the Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector; the Three Dukes; and the Director of the Department of State Affairs—each with ten vermilion-robed direct attendants; the Three Dukes' attendants were called Direct Office.
三師 is the triad 太師、太傅、太保, distinct from 三公; the fused Three Excellencies wording conflates those groups.

First rank, positive: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector; Three Dukes; Director of the Department of State Affairs—ten vermilion-robed direct attendants each; the Three Dukes were called Direct Office.

First rank, positive: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, and Grand Protector; Three Dukes; Director of the Department of State Affairs—ten vermilion-robed direct attendants each; the Three Dukes' attendants were called Direct Office.
硃衣直省…三公稱直府 names the Three Dukes' attendant corps Direct Office; it does not rename the dukes themselves.

First negative rank: the Left and Right Chancellors, Commissioners for Pacification and Administration, Commander-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs—with the same direct attendants; the Bureau called them Direct Court, filled by duty attendants.

First negative rank: the Left and Right Chancellors, Managers of Governmental Affairs, Commander-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs—with the same direct attendants; the Bureau called them Direct Court, filled by duty attendants.
平章政事 is Manager of Governmental Affairs; Commissioners for Pacification and Administration would be 招討, which is not in this unit.

First rank, negative: Left and Right Chancellors of the Department of State Affairs, Commissioners for Pacification and Administration, Commander-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs—direct attendants the same; the Bureau of Military Affairs called them Direct Court, filled by attendants on duty.

First rank, negative: Left and Right Chancellors of the Department of State Affairs, Managers of Governmental Affairs, Commander-in-Chief, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs—direct attendants the same; the Bureau of Military Affairs called them Direct Court, filled by attendants on duty.
The literal has the same 平章政事 error; Managers of Governmental Affairs is the office listed after the chancellors.

Third positive rank: the Eastern Palace Three Juniors, Army Supervisors of the Commander-in-Chief, Chief Palace Inspector, Ministers of the Six Ministries, capital guardians, Palace Proclamation Commissioner, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, Hanlin Academician Expositor, and equivalent offices—each with six reception escorts and twenty carriage-handlers.

Third positive rank: the Eastern Palace Three Juniors, Army Supervisors of the Commander-in-Chief, Chief Palace Inspector, Ministers of the Six Ministries, capital guardians, Palace Proclamation Commissioner, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, and equivalent offices—each with six reception escorts and twenty carriage-handlers.
翰林學士承旨 is Recipient of Edicts; expositor would be 侍講, which is not written here.

Third rank, positive: Eastern Palace Three Juniors, Left and Right Army Supervisors of the Commander-in-Chief, Chief Palace Inspector, Ministers of the Six Ministries, capital guardians, Palace Proclamation Commissioner, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, Hanlin Academician Expositor, and all offices of the same rank—each six reception escorts and twenty carriage-handlers.

Third rank, positive: Eastern Palace Three Juniors, Left and Right Army Supervisors of the Commander-in-Chief, Chief Palace Inspector, Ministers of the Six Ministries, capital guardians, Palace Proclamation Commissioner, Commissioner for Encouraging Agriculture, Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, and all offices of the same rank—each six reception escorts and twenty carriage-handlers.
The literal likewise misnames 承旨 as expositor; Recipient of Edicts matches the title.

Fourth positive rank: Left and Right Remonstrance Grandees, Director of the Directorate of Education, Vice Ministers of the Six Ministries, and equivalent offices—each with eight reception escorts, reduced from the original twelve.

Fourth positive rank: Left and Right Remonstrance Grandees, Director of the Directorate of Education, Vice Ministers of the Six Ministries, and equivalent offices—each with eight reception escorts and twelve personal attendants.
各引接八人，本破十二人 are two parallel complements; 本破 is the Jin personal-attendant class, not a reduction from twelve.

Fourth rank, positive: Left and Right Remonstrance Grand Masters, Director of the Directorate of Education, Vice Ministers of the Six Ministries, and all offices of the same rank—each eight reception escorts, originally twelve.

Fourth rank, positive: Left and Right Remonstrance Grand Masters, Director of the Directorate of Education, Vice Ministers of the Six Ministries, and all offices of the same rank—each eight reception escorts and twelve personal attendants.
本破 is not the adverb originally; the unit assigns eight reception escorts and twelve personal attendants.

Fourth negative rank: Left and Right Palace Guard Generals, all meng'an chiliarchs, princely mansion commandants, and capital transport vice commissioners, and equivalent offices—each with four reception escorts, reduced from twelve personal attendants.

Fourth negative rank: Left and Right Palace Guard Generals, all meng'an chiliarchs, princely mansion commandants, and capital transport vice commissioners, and equivalent offices—each with four reception escorts and twelve personal attendants.
各引接四人，本破十二人 are concurrent allotments, not a cut from twelve to four.

Fourth rank, negative: Left and Right Palace Guard Generals, all meng'an chiliarchs, princely mansion commandants, and capital transport vice commissioners, and all offices of the same rank—each four reception escorts, originally twelve personal attendants.

Fourth rank, negative: Left and Right Palace Guard Generals, all meng'an chiliarchs, princely mansion commandants, and capital transport vice commissioners, and all offices of the same rank—each four reception escorts and twelve personal attendants.
本破十二人 names twelve personal attendants alongside four reception escorts.

Translators and interpreters of the Department of State Affairs and Bureau of Military Affairs, interpreters of the Six Ministries, Censorate, and Army Supervisory Office, edict-office clerks, National History Institute copyists, and similar posts—each had one personal attendant.

Clerks, translators, and interpreters of the Department of State Affairs and the Bureau of Military Affairs; interpreters of the Six Ministries, Censorate, and Army Supervisory Office; edict-office clerks; National History Institute copyists; and similar posts—each had one personal attendant.
尚書省樞密院令譯史通事 abbreviates 令史、譯史、通事; omitting clerks drops 令史 from the source list.
Public envoys and personal manpower for Posu were filled by recruiting Han commoners near Eastern Capital and Chenzhou.
Public envoys and personal manpower for Posu were filled by recruiting Han commoners near the Eastern Capital, Chengzhou.
附近東京澄州 is Chengzhou near the Eastern Capital, one recruiting locale, not Eastern Capital and a separate Chenzhou (陳州).
Public envoys and personal manpower for Posu were recruited from Han commoners near Eastern Capital Chenzhou to fill the posts.
Public envoys and personal manpower for Posu were recruited from Han commoners near the Eastern Capital, Chengzhou, to fill the posts.
澄州 is Chengzhou; Chenzhou romanizes a different prefecture.
Death requiring return escort received half again; those who retired or were dismissed before age sixty received none.
If death required a return escort, the grant was further reduced by half; those who retired or were dismissed before age sixty received none.

又減半給之 further halves the half-grant of the preceding retired-official rule; the original half again is the wrong arithmetic, and the proposed were granted after a further reduction by half is ungrammatical.
For death requiring return escort, half was given again; if retirement or dismissal came before age sixty, none was granted.
For those whose death required a return escort, the grant was further reduced by half; if retirement or dismissal came before age sixty, none was granted.
減半給之 is a further reduction by half, not giving half again; the proposed literal is accurate and grammatical.
